articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Prayer Day is an Event which occurs when the player outpost is within 2,000 meters of a Holy Nation location, and not within a no-go zone. Its initiating event will have up to a 50% chance each day of triggering, if you are based 1,500 meters or closer to a Holy Nation owned location. The chance will scale down with distance, reaching 0% chance at 2,000 meters or more. It consists of a squad of 5 High Paladins and 4 Holy Servants led by a Holy Priest, the last of which will require an audience to pray with you. The conditions for fulfilling the prayer day are the following: Have at least 1 male in the squad. Have The Holy Flame in inventory. Interact with the Priest as a Human. In case of lacking The Holy Flame, the priest will provide a copy the very first time for free. This limit is per game, not character. If the player fails the condition, a Holy Nation Assault (Minor) will be later launched aimed at evicting the player from their lands. Interacting as a non-human counts as an insult, it will be launched in 10 ~ 20 hours. If the player attacks the priest, it will be launched in 12 ~ 24 hours. If all characters are female, it will be launched in 12 ~ 36 hours (this specific variant can be pacified by recruiting a male character). If ignored for way too long, or the interaction goes poorly, it will be launched is 36 ~ 48 hours. As soon as the Prayer Day is done another one should appear on the “Events” page and will launch in 100 to 160 hours. This event will stop happening if any of the following is true: An enemy of the Holy Nation, Allied with either the Flotsam Ninjas or the Shek Kingdom Phoenix has been killed or imprisoned. Arguably, out of all of the major factions, the Prayer Day is the least damaging of “Tax” Events to a player, as the Holy Nation only takes to show a token of loyalty and a little bit of player’s time. The Shek Kingdom and the United Cities hurt the player in much more substantial ways. Like most tax Events, if the campaign is defeated by a third-party faction like bandits or wild animals on the way to the player’s outpost, it will prevent any future tax visits from the faction until the player’s next import. This is due to the long repeat limit timer, and the fact that it doesn’t consider being defeated by a third party as the player killing them. This can be exploited by purposefully luring hostiles to the event’s forces while they en route to the player’s base. Prayer Oh Okran, Lord of Light… Let thine flame burneth bright… With this blessed body most pure… Let us not be tempted by the Shadow’s lure Let us not yearn for fleshly pleasure… But yearn only for love from the Creator… Let us honour our sacred brothers… Let us abstain from intoxications… For darkness preys on the idle mind… Let us pray for the wellbeing of all mankind. In faith. Trivia Due to the fact that the dialogue check doesn’t actually account whether the male character inside the squad is a human or not, one could potentially fulfill the condition of prayer day even if all their male squad members are Sheks, Hivers, or even Skeletons.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: It's that time of the week again, my favourite day... tax day. Don't keep me waiting now...Samurai Sergeant The Tax Collector is an Event sent by United Cities to collect taxes from players that have agreed to pay taxes in the Tax Man Visit or Tax Collector events, or as a result of losing the Tax Evasion Enforcement event. It cannot trigger if the player is an ally of the Anti-Slavers or United Cities, an enemy of the United Cities, or if Emperor Tengu is killed or captured. Once triggered, the United Cities will send a campaign to the player’s base. This campaign will consist of 1 squad, made up of 3-6 Samurai and led by a Samurai Sergeant. Once the campaign arrives, the sergeant will begin shouting at the player to come speak with them, failing to do so will result in a Tax Evasion Enforcement event being triggered in 48-72 hours if this event originally triggered from you agreeing to pay taxes, or 24-60 hours if this event was a response to failing a previous Tax Evasion Enforcement event. When speaking to the sergeant, they will insult your outpost if it is less than level 2 (Watchtower icon), then demand you pay c.3,000, with a chance to increase the taxes to c.4,500 if Tinfist is still alive and free. Or, if this event was triggered in response to failing a Tax Evasion Enforcement event, you will be demanded to pay c.6,000 thanks to a ‘late payment’ and ‘administration fees’. Agreeing to pay the taxes will result in 140-160 hours, while refusal will result in a Tax Evasion Enforcement event in 60-72 hours. Like most tax Events, if the campaign is defeated by a third-party faction like bandits or wild animals on the way to the player’s outpost, it will prevent any future tax visits from the faction until the player’s next import. This is due to the long repeat limit timer, and the fact that it doesn’t consider being defeated by a third party as the player killing them. This can be exploited by purposefully luring hostiles to the event’s forces while they en route to the player’s base.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Right then pansies, here's your options... Pay us 2,000 of your coins every 2 days. Then we become best friends, and no Dust Bandits will attack you. Like best friends do. Or, don't pay us anything, I go tell the boss that you don't want to be friends, and then we loot the shit out of your little outpost here.Dust Boss Bandit Demands is an event sent by the Dust Bandits to extort money from players who settle near their territory. It can trigger as long as the player has a base within 4,500 meters of one of their locations or camps, and the Dust King is not dead (unlike many World States this means actually dead, not just imprisoned). It will have a 20% chance each day to trigger if the player’s base is within 2,000 meters of a location or camp owned by the Dust Bandits, this chance will scale down with distance until it hits 0% chance at 4,500 meters away. Once triggered, the Dust Bandits will send a campaign to the player’s base. This campaign will consist of one or two squads, each made up of 6-10 Dust Bandits, 1-4 Dust Bandit Bowmen, and led by a Dust Boss. When the campaign arrives the War Leader will begin shouting at the player to come speak with them. If spoken to, the Bandits will demand that the player pay c.2,000 to avoid being attacked. If the player agrees to pay, another Bandit Demands event will be triggered in 42-56 hours. If the player ignores them or refuses to pay, the campaign will assault the player’s outpost, breaking gates and attacking any player characters they come across. If the assault is defeated, another Bandit Demands event has a 50% chance to trigger in 50-80 hours. If the assault defeats the player, a new Bandit Demands event will be triggered in 40-50 hours. In the dialog with the War Leader, the player also has an option to stab the War Leader. If this is done, the campaign will immediately retreat, and a Bandit Rage event will trigger in 20-50 hours. Unlike most tax events, this event cannot be avoided by having the forces killed by a third party, as this event has a short repeat limit cooldown. Even if slain by a third party, it will simply come again later.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: WHAT IS THIS!?!? An invasion! A rival colony come to do battle, crab against crab! So be it! We shall test each others crab training skills! It's a crab toouuurrrrnameeeennntttt!!!Crab Raider Overview The Crab Tournaments are a series of events involving the Crab Raiders faction. They trigger when a Crab Raider spots a player character inside a base owned by the player, and the faction reputation with them is less than 50. The Crab Queen must also still be in power. Over the course of the events, several raids will attack your base, including a number of unique crabs. It is impossible to truly lose the tournament, as it just loops on itself if you repeatedly lose the rounds of the tournament. Achieving victory in the final round of the tournament will result in gaining an alliance with the Crab Raiders faction. Despite being implied to be a battle between crabs, you don’t actually need any crabs or even animals to participate. The raiders will simply refer to your crab as the “Mystery Crab” throughout the tournament regardless of if you have one or not. Variants Once spotted by a Crab Raider patrol, the first event Crab Tournament will be triggered in 12-32 hours. Crab Tournament The first round of the tournament, consisting of 8-12 Crab Raiders, 10 Crabs, and Titus. If the raiders are defeated, the Crab Quarter Finals event will be triggered in 72-120 hours. If the raiders are victorious, the first round will trigger again in 72-120 hours. Crab Quarter Finals The second round of the tournament, consisting of 12-15 Crab Raiders, 10 Crabs, and Barnabus. If the raiders are defeated, the Crab Semi Finals event will be triggered in 72-100 hours. If the raiders are victorious, the Crab Remedial Round event will be triggered in 72-100 hours. Crab Semi Finals The third round of the tournament, consisting of 14-21 Crab Raiders, 15 Crabs, and Mr Gigantus. If the raiders are defeated, the Crab Tournament Final event will be triggered in 70-140 hours. If the raiders are victorious, the Crab Remedial Round event will be triggered in 72-120 hours. Crab Tournament Final The fourth and final round of the tournament, consisting of 20-25 Crab Raiders, 15 Crabs, and The Crabinator. If the raiders are defeated, the Crab Champion event will be triggered in 1 hour. If the raiders are victorious, the Crab Remedial Round event will be triggered in 72-120 hours. Crab Remedial Round A special round of the tournament, which only triggers if the player is defeated in one of the rounds of the tournament. It consists of 8-10 Crab Raiders and 10 Crabs. If the raiders are defeated, the Crab Quarter Finals event will be triggered again in 72-100 hours. If the raiders are victorious, the Crab Remedial Round event will be triggered again in 72-100 hours. Crab Champion The final event in the tournament, which consists of 8-10 Crab Raiders and 10 Crabs but is non-hostile. Once it arrives, they will give a short speech announcing the player’s “Mystery Crab” as the grand champion of the tournament, instantly allying the player to the Crab Raiders faction. Shortly afterwards the raiders will take their leave and return home. Tips and bugs It is possible to lower your standing with the Crab Raiders in a controlled way to below 50 by repeatedly and unsuccessfully attempting a sneak knockout on the Crab Queen. This is useful if you have more than 50 relations already but still want the Crab Tournament to happen. Dropping the reputation to 49 in this way will anger the whole throne room. The terrain in Crab Raider territory is rocky and uneven. This causes the bigger crabs to get stuck easily. It may be necessary to leave the base to intercept the stuck crabs in order to complete a tournament round successfully. A war party will typically spawn in at the closest Crab Village. Building close to it may reduce the AI path finding troubles. It is possible for the Crab Tournament to trigger on NPC factions, if they happen to have a squad in the player’s town and a Crab Raider patrol spots them. As the dialog only checks if they are in a player owned town, not if the character they see is a player.

Charmed!Elite Hunter War Leader Elite Hunter Assault is an event that can trigger from being an enemy of the United Cities and living within 9,000 meters of a United Cities location, or as a response to defeating the Elite Hunter Assault, Eyegore’s Assault, or Noble’s Wrath Assault. At least one noble from the following list must be alive and free to trigger the event: Emperor Tengu, Lord Inaba, Lord Nagata, Lord Yoshinaga, Lady Sanda, Lady Tsugi. If all the nobles listed are killed or captured, the event will be unable to trigger except as a response to defeating Elite Hunter Assault. When triggered, the United Cities will launch an assault on the player’s base. This assault will consist of 3-5 Elite Hunters, led by an additional Elite Hunter. When the assault arrives, the leader will give a short speech introducing themselves, and then they will attack the player’s gates and characters. If victorious, the assault will leave shortly afterward. If defeated, there is a chance to trigger the Eyegore’s Assault event, or another Elite Hunter Assault. The chance for each varies depending on the source of this event. If triggered as a territorial event, Eyegore’s Assault will have a 20% chance to trigger in 72-100 hours, while Elite Hunter Assault will have a 20% chance to trigger in 72-100 hours. If triggered in response to defeating a variant of Noble’s Wrath Assault that is triggered by killing/capturing a noble, or defeating Eyegore’s Assault, Eyegore’s Assault will have a 40% chance to trigger in 72-100 hours assuming Eyegore has not been killed or captured, and Elite Hunter Assault will have a 20% chance to trigger in 72-100 hours. If triggered as response to defeating a special dialogue triggered variant of the Noble’s Wrath Assault event, only the Elite Hunter Assault can trigger as a response, and will have a 60% chance to trigger in 72-144 hours. This next one will also have the same chances if defeated, and the next one, and so on. And if triggered in response to defeating the Elite Hunter Assault, except as mentioned above in the Noble’s Wrath Assault dialogue trigger variant, Eyegore’s Assault will have a 35% chance to trigger in 72-144 hours, and Elite Hunter Assault will have a 25% chance to trigger in 72-144 hours.

Base Assaults are a scrapped system that has since been replaced. You can find the new version on the Events page. Base Assaults were an attack on the player’s outpost where an army of a faction raids the player’s outpost to either attack the inhabitants or steal resources and items. It was introduced in version 0.60.0. If there are no player characters in a base during an assault, then the invading group will wait outside until someone returns before attacking. Causes of base assault Base assaults occur when players are hostile with a faction or, if the player is being extorted out of their Cats via racketeering or taxing, base assault can happen if the player refuses to pay the faction. Sometimes base assaults can just be random. Once the faction enters the outpost with their army, the player has a few minutes to interact with them, which gives them a few options to coerce them to cease the base assault, such as bribing them by giving up all the funds or half of them, if persuaded. If the player doesn’t interact the invading army for a while, they will automatically attack and raid the player’s outpost of their items and resources. If there are any of the player’s squad members, the army will attack them first before looting the outpost. Attacking the invading army after bribing them with valuables will not recover them. Major factions (The Holy Nation, United Cities, and Shek Kingdom) will assault your base when relations become negative enough or if your actions trigger one. History Dust Bandits - Introduced in version 0.60.0. Starving Bandits - Introduced in version 0.62.0. Cannibals - Introduced in version 0.62.0.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Loading screen tip: If you set up base too near to other outposts, cannibal villages or bandit camps, be prepared for the consequences. Anticipated or ongoing Events can be found on the right side of the Factions window. Events include scheduled visits to a player’s outpost by another faction and ongoing Bodyguard Jobs. The timer will show how much time is left until an event starts or the time left on a Bodyguard job. Information regarding only one bodyguard job will be presented at a time, although the player can have multiple bodyguards hired at once. In contrast, several different visits can be scheduled and listed in the Events list. Bodyguards Bodyguards are characters that are set to guard members of your faction or your outpost for a limited amount of time. They can either be hired or will join you as allies out of their own free will. Once you have acquired a bodyguard, an Event will be shown under the Faction tab stating the number of hours before they leave. Some bodyguards, depending on personality, may stay longer if all members of the player’s squad are KOed upon expiry of contract. For a full list of characters capable of being bodyguards, see Bodyguards. Mercenaries Mercenaries are bodyguards that are usually hired at bars using cats. They usually give a choice between bodyguarding the player or their nearest outpost. Mercenary Guild - after talking to a Mercenary Captain or a Human Mercenary squad leader. The Human Mercenary variant is only found in The Holy Nation. They cost c.1,000 per day up to two days to guard the player, and c.2,000 every two days up to eight days to guard the player’s outpost. Tech Hunters - after talking to a Drifter squad leader of this faction that are found in bars. They cost the same as normal mercenaries. Cannibal Hunters - after talking to a Cannibal Hunter squad leader. They cost c.3,000 per day to guard the player, and c.3,000 every two days up to eight days to guard the player’s outpost. Black Dogs - after talking to a Black Dog Bodyguard trying to extort the player. They cost c.2,500 per day to guard the player, and upon completion of the contract will demand an exit fee of c.700 or can be re-hired. Note that refusing to pay the exit fee or not hiring them in the first place will cause them to attack. They also have a unique bodyguard event where they show up at a player’s outpost to extort protection. This will cost c.4,000 for two days but can be lowered down to c.3,500 or c.3,000. Allies If a player has allied with these factions, some of their patrols can be asked to follow the player or may randomly follow the player on their own. Anti-Slavers - if Big Bo is in the squad, she will sometimes hail Anti-Slaver squads for three days (interestingly may include Tinfist’s squad //confirm). Alternatively, if the player has taken down any high-ranking UC leader or noble groups, random Anti-Slaver squads will also bodyguard the player for three days. Crab Raiders - random protection from Crab Raider patrols. They will guard the crabbed for 6 hours. Flotsam Ninjas - after showing Note From Moll to Flotsam Ninja squad leaders consisting of more than 4 individuals in a patrol. Rebel Farmers - after speaking to a patrolling Rebel Farmer squad leader. If the option implying importance they will bodyguard the player for three days, else they may refuse or only bodyguard the player for one day. Rebel Swordsmen - after speaking to a Rebel Captain squad leader that is not guarding a town. They will bodyguard the player for one day. Shek Kingdom - after speaking to a Hundred Guardian squad leader that is not guarding a town. They will bodyguard the player for 3 days or defend the player’s outpost for two days. Starving Bandits - after giving food to the leader of patrol (don’t expect them to last long). The Holy Nation - showing the Holy Seal to a Paladin patrol leader. They will bodyguard the player for 36 hours. United Cities - random protection from patrols, usually led by a Samurai Sergeant (Samurai Rogues can technically bodyguard the player, if they are somehow allied to UC while the conditions for Rogues to spawn are met). They will bodyguard the player for three days. Other Unique bodyguard events with special “contract” conditions. Tech Hunter Ruins - if the player finds a lone tech hunter near ancient ruins, they may be able to talk to them. Accepting their company will cause them to bodyguard the player for 24 hours. Error_Code_0xFFFFFF - after being seen by them. They ally themselves to the player character that saw them with a bodyguard “contract” that lasts over a hundred in-game years. Types of Outpost Visits/Assaults Major factions visit the player’s outpost for a multitude of reasons. The most common reason for a visit is when a major faction establishes that another settlement has sprung up in previously barren land and that it has to be included in their sphere of influence. Each major faction will send representatives of their government to demand a token of loyalty of a new settlement to their authority. Should this gesture of obedience be refused, the major powers will then visit player’s outpost for a second reason - to destroy and pillage the upstart criminal. Some of these assaults can only be stopped by destroying the key figures of the major power that sends them. Destroying key figures will bring about their own special “visit” events in retaliation. Typically, the assaults compose of a faction sending a small fraction of their army force as a platoon to the player base, which tend to increase in size (with a few exceptions[1]) and difficulty for each previous one defeated until the largest assaults that commonly happen as a result of defeating their key leaders. Sometimes important leaders (Such as Eyegore and Esata) may also personally lead the platoon into assault, the size and scale of which the leader leads can also differ drastically between the trigger used. Many of these assaults can be repetitive, potentially infinitely, and tend to be re-launched every few days or weeks. How visits trigger Each faction checks for a new event every 6 in-game hours. A faction runs one event at a time. While one is running or scheduled, it won’t roll another. Your base must be within the event’s range of one of the faction’s towns. The closer, the more likely. Past the max range, never. One of your characters must be at the base. Events don’t target empty bases. A scheduled event whose base is empty waits or switches to another of your bases, and is eventually cancelled. Some events need a minimum number of characters, counted across all your squads (listed below). Each event has a cooldown before it can happen again. Many first visits (Tax Man Visit, Traders Guild Visit, Prayer Day, Tribute Round, Hound’s Welcome) only roll once per game. Later visits are follow-ups. Follow-ups (return visits, assaults after you refuse) are scheduled by your dialogue choice or by how the event ended. They show in the Events list with a timer. Your base’s level doesn’t matter, except for the Shek Tribute Round. Two options affect these events: Town raid events: frequency (0.25x to 3x) scales how likely events are. Caravan events ignore it. Town raid events: size (0.25x to 4x) scales how big events are. Size is counted in characters: whole squads are added until the size is reached. Your base’s level or wealth doesn’t change it. The Holy Nation Holy Assault - Suppression event, having hostile relations with the faction. Holy Nation Assault (Minor) - Suppression event, numerous sources including failing Prayer Day, having no men at the outpost, or having non-humans (and without being pacified). Holy Nation Assault (Major) - Retaliation event, defeating Holy Assault, Holy Nation Assault (Minor), or Holy Nation Assault (Major) events. Holy Nation Assault (Inquisitor) - Retaliation event, defeating Holy Nation Assault (Major) event. Prayer Day - Tax event, living near the faction’s territory. Retribution of God - Retaliation event, defeating Seta, Valtena, or both. Wrath of God - Retaliation event, kill or kidnap the Phoenix. Defeating Retribution of God. United Cities Drug Bust - Getting caught growing or processing Hemp. Elite Hunter Assault - Suppression event, having hostile relations with the faction. Eyegore’s Assault - Retaliation event, defeating Longen or Tengu. Noble’s Wrath - Retaliation event, harming, stealing from, or disrespecting a noble. Noble’s Wrath Assault - Retaliation event, killing a noble. Tax Collector - Tax event, accepting to pay taxes in Tax Collector or Tax Man Visit event, or failing a Tax Evasion Enforcement event. A new collector is dispatched every 140-160 hours (about a week) while you keep paying. Tax Evasion Enforcement - Suppression event, refusing to pay taxes in Tax Collector or Tax Man Visit events. Dispatched 24-72 hours after you refuse. Tax Man Visit - Tax event, living near the faction’s territory. United Cities Assault - Retaliation event, defeating Drug Bust or Tax Evasion Enforcement events. Shek Kingdom Enemy Hunt - Suppression event, having hostile relations with the faction. Invincible Vengeance - Retaliation event, defeating Esata. Return For Blood - Suppression event, refusing to provide tribute in the Tribute Round or Return For Tribute events. Dispatched 12-30 hours after you refuse. Return For Tribute - Tax event, accepting to provide tribute in the Tribute Round event. A new visit is dispatched every 100-250 hours while you keep paying. Shek Challengers - Retaliation event, defeating Enemy Hunt, Return For Blood, Return For Tribute, Shek Revenge, or Tribute Round events. Shek Revenge - Retaliation event, defeating Enemy Hunt, Invincible Vengeance, Shek Challengers, Shek Revenge, or Stone Golem’s Revenge events. Stone Golem’s Revenge - Retaliation event, defeating Bayan or Seto. Tribute Round - Tax event, living near the faction’s territory, with a level 1+ base and 5+ characters. Minor Factions Minor factions will visit the player’s outpost for either taxing, raiding, or trading. They can also send retaliatory events after the player affects a world state. Tax Events Bandit Demands - Dust Bandits, living near the faction’s territory. Hound Check In - Hounds, living near the faction’s territory while allied. Hound’s Welcome - Hounds, living near the faction’s territory. Stone Rat Visit - Stone Rats, living near the faction’s territory. Traders Guild Visit - Traders Guild, living near the faction’s territory, with 3+ characters. Caravan Events Caravan events ignore the raid frequency option. Beast Trader - Nomads, living near the faction’s territory. Caravan Visit - Traders Guild, living near the faction’s territory. Farm Trader - Western Hive, living near the faction’s territory. Materials Trader - Western Hive, living near the faction’s territory. Unprovoked Attack Events Bandit Raid - Black Dragon Ninjas, living near the faction’s territory. Blooded Raid - Reavers, living near the faction’s territory, with 4+ characters. Cannibal Raid - Cannibals, living near the faction’s territory, with 5+ characters. Coast Raid - Fishmen, living near the faction’s territory (currently unable to trigger due to the fact that their faction is “not real”). Crab Tournament - Crab Raiders, having your base spotted by members of the faction. Crabbed Ones - Crab Raiders, living near the faction’s territory. Mighty Canhead - Cannibals, living near the faction’s territory, with 6+ characters. Ninja Raid - Sand Ninjas, living near the faction’s territory. Raid - Band of Bones, living near the faction’s territory. Red Sabre Raid - Red Sabres, living near the faction’s territory, with 3+ characters. Scrawny Raid - Cannibals, living near the faction’s territory, with 5+ characters. Shek Proving - Kral’s Chosen, living near their territory. Skin Harvest - Skin Bandits, living near the faction’s territory. Slave Raid - Slave Traders, living near the faction’s territory, with 5+ characters. Southern Hive Visit - Southern Hive, living near the faction’s territory. The Big Skin Harvest - Skin Bandits, living near the faction’s territory or defeating the Skin Harvest event. The Fog - Fogmen, living near the faction’s territory, with 5+ characters. Retaliation Events Bandit Rage - Dust Bandits, stabbing the Dust Boss during the Bandit Demands event. Cannibal Swarm - Cannibals, defeating the Cannibal Raid or Scrawny Raid events. Challenger of the Undefeated - Berserkers, defeating the Bugmaster. Hive Attack - Southern Hive, kidnapping the Queen of the South. Hive Attack - Western Hive, kidnapping The Queen. Hive Eviction - Southern Hive, defeating the Southern Hive Visit event. Jonin Assault - Anti-Slavers, defeating Bo, Jaeger, and Grey, or defeating Tinfist. Revenge of the Hounds - Hounds, having hostile relations with the faction, or defeating Big Grim. The hostile-relations version has a range of 0 in the game data, so it never triggers on its own. Shek Challenge - Kral’s Chosen, defeating the Bugmaster, Esata the Stone Golem, or Holy Lord Phoenix. Shek Challengers - Band of Bones, defeating a Raid or Shek Challengers event. Slave Capture - Slave Traders, harboring escaped slaves. Stone Rat Assault - Stone Rats, defeating Stone Rat Assault or Stone Rat Visit events. Thug Attack - United Heroes League, refusing to pay membership fees in Traders Guild Visit event, or defeating the Thug Attack event. Types of Outpost Visits/Assaults: Ally Reinforcements Some allied factions have reinforcement events, which will trigger in response to certain hostile events from mutual enemy factions. They will attempt to reach your base before the incoming hostile event does, though they may fail if their own territory is too far away. If more than one allied reinforcement event is valid for a specific hostile event, all valid allied reinforcements will be sent. Anti-Slaver Reinforcements - Triggering the Eyegore’s Assault, Noble’s Wrath, or Noble’s Wrath Assault events. Flotsam Ninja Reinforcements - Triggering the Holy Assault, Holy Nation Assault (Inquisitor), Retribution of God, or Wrath of God events. Holy Nation Reinforcements - Triggering the Enemy Hunt, Invincible Vengeance, or Stone Golem’s Revenge events. Hound Reinforcements - Triggering the Bandit Raid or Red Sabre Raid events. Rebel Farmers Reinforcements - Triggering the Eyegore’s Assault, Noble’s Wrath, or Noble’s Wrath Assault events. Shek Kingdom Reinforcements - Triggering the Eyegore’s Assault, Holy Assault, Holy Nation Assault (Inquisitor), Noble’s Wrath, Noble’s Wrath Assault, Retribution Of God, or Wrath Of God events. United Cities Reinforcements - Triggering the Holy Assault, Holy Nation Assault (Inquisitor), Jonin Assault, Retribution Of God, or Wrath Of God events. Types of Outpost Visits/Assaults: Base Attacks Base Attacks are not technically part of the events system, but have similar interactions with player bases. They are wandering squads that spawn in the wilderness, and actively seek out and assault player owned bases if they are nearby. Sometimes these can also be affected by world states, generally the killing or capturing of said faction’s leader or leaders will stop these types of squads from spawning, though rarely it is the status of other faction’s characters. A base attack only starts if: the base has a gate. Bases without a gate never get base attacks; one of your characters is within 2,500 units of the base; the squad isn’t allied with you; that faction’s cooldown has passed. The Town attacks frequency option sets the cooldown: how long each faction waits after its last base attack ends before it can attack again. The raid frequency and size options don’t affect base attacks. The following factions have squads with this behavior: Band of Bones Black Dragon Ninjas Crab Raiders Dust Bandits Gorrillo Bandits Grass Pirates Rebel Farmers Red Sabres Shrieking Bandits Skeleton Bandits Skeleton Legion Southern Hive Spiders Starving Bandits Swamp Ninjas Thrall Masters Vagrants Western Hive (Only after death or capture of The Queen) Wolves Yabuta Outlaws (Only after Yabuta of the Sands is freed)

This section will compose of all the factions that have World States which could increase their influence inside Kenshi’s factions, though it should be noted that not all of them have quests or can be reasoned with (such as the Reavers), and even those with quests may not necessarily target all the individuals that might be of interest to them. This article will serve as the hub for all the factions that have potential to increase their influence in the world, as long as they are shown in the faction tab. The following factions have their routes: Major Factions The Holy Nation United Cities Shek Kingdom Traders Guild Minor Factions Kral’s Chosen Flotsam Ninjas Rebel Farmers Anti-Slavers Crab Raiders Reavers Skeleton Bandits Skin Bandits Southern Hive

The Phoenix and his two inquisitors, Seta and Valtena, form a strong defensive triangle between the three of them. The High Inquisitors fortify the enemy perimeters, but take them out and the Holy Nation will start to crack.Moll Flotsam Ninjas Route is a World State Route where the player has allied relationship with Flotsam Ninjas and initiated dialogue with Moll that opens up the questline for HN to change the state of Kenshi in a way that advances the FN’s interests. To talk with Moll, the player must be allied with FN. The goal of this questline mainly revolves around taking down The Holy Nation leaders and instigating revolutions to topple down the regime of HN. Main Targets (This part includes the targets that are directly referenced by the questline) Seta controls Stack in the south west of the plains. Valtena you'll find in a military outpost, Okran's Shield, on the eastern border. Do not underestimate their hold on the Holy Nation, the two of them are probably smarter than the Phoenix himself - he was born into his role, remember, but those guys earned it with pure Okranite crazy and cunning.Moll While there aren’t any strict priorities in which you take down The Holy Nation leaders, Flotsam’s plan mainly revolves around taking down the 2 High Inquisitors, Seta and Valtena, before they march upon Blister Hill and take down the Phoenix. There are a few differences in dialogue depending on whether you take down Phoenix, Seta, or Valtena first. The people of Blister Hill couldn't handle the downfall of their 'invincible' god lord. I guess you've seen the ruins, (player name)?Moll, Phoenix down first, Seta and/or Valtena alive Whew, (player name), you really did a number on Stack!And it looks like we weren't the only ones waiting to attack the Holy Nation. They've got their hands full fending off the Shek from the south after the defences were left open... A perfect distraction while we attack Okran's Shield, don't you think? Taking out Valtena will hit their military numbers even more so that we can finally take back Blister Hill...Moll, Seta down first, Phoenix and Valtena alive Whew, (player name), you really did a number on Okran's Shield!!While the military are still regrouping and licking their wounds, this is our chance to stir things up. Next we take out their southern defensive position: Stack.Moll, Valtena down first, Phoenix and Seta alive Once you take down both Inquisitors, Flotsam Patrols will start spawning in Okran’s Valley and Okran’s Gulf, this is when they will be finally strong enough to take down HN. The inquisitors are officially out of the Holy Nation!This is it, (player name), the Phoenix' oppression is finally over and he's quaking in his holy boots... We're coming for him. We're ready to take back Blister Hill. The Valleys of Okran belong to the people now... Thanks to you, /YOURNAME/...And me, of course... *snort* The reign of the Holy Nation had to end some day. I'm just glad you and I could be the ones to do it... Rot in the abyss, Phoenix.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Shek Kingdom Route is a World State Route where the player has allied relationship with Shek Kingdom and initiated dialogue with Esata the Stone Golem that opens up the questline for SK to change the state of Kenshi that advances SK’s interests. The SK route is diametrically opposed to The Holy Nation Route. The goal of this questline mainly revolves around destroying The Holy Nation by getting rid of all 3 of their leaders. In order to initiate dialogue with Esata, the player should be either allied (+50) relations, or be at least above (+35) relations, and having killed/imprisoned either Bugmaster or Phoenix. Once that is done, the following lines will be stated by Esata, depending on what condition the player has achieved. (Player Name), you did what I could not… The Bugmaster/Phoenix mutt is finally dead/defeated by your sword. Reverence. To the Shek, you are no longer an outsider… You are our kin. (+60 relations with SK) This day, I name you a warrior of Kral, an honorary Invincible… (Player Name) The Battle Born! (+10 relations with SK) Honor to (Player Name)! (Shek rally for applause) Honor to the Battle Born! *Battlecries* Let it be known! An enemy of the Invincible Battle Born is an enemy of the Shek! +20 relations with SK, -15 relations with HN She would also give you Seto. Favour, Battle Born… Take my daughter, Seto. Teach her. My blood is hers. She’ll prove her worth to you. Trust. “Seto. Well met, (Player Name).” - Seto Seto Joins Squad Main Targets (This part includes the targets that are directly referenced by the questline) After the initial opening lines are spoken, the player will unlock further dialogues with the Esata. To do so, the player simply has to reinitiate dialogue with Esata, and tell her that you wish to destroy The Holy Nation. This will give +20 relations with Shek Kingdom and unlock the dialogue with Esata on HN. [Shes glares at you and the room falls silent with anticipation]... You will not fight this fight without the Shek Kingdom... We fight with you, Battle Born First, we hit Seta of Stack and take the town as ours. My warriors will want to fight by your side. Ask them. Do not deprive them of the battle they deserve, do you hear me? Then we lay siege to the grass plains and take Valtena of Okran's Shield with it. The Phoenix mutt falls last, only after he has watched his nation collapse under his feet. What do you say of this plan, Battle Born?Esata the Stone Golem It doesn’t really matter whether you agree on or follow up with Esata’s plan, but for the sake of simplicity we will assume that you went with her plan. Hm hm hm! The Okranite cattle are so weak and cowardly when they have no leader to herd them. Taking Stack and Bad Teeth was easy with Seta of Stack defeated. My warriors continue their war with the surviving Okranite dogs of the south...Valtena of the East is still left for taking. I must hold our ground here, but lead my warriors to Okran's Shield...Esata the Stone Golem Stack and Bad Teeth get overtaken by Shek Kingdom after Seta is defeated, HN army also decreases in frequency in Okran’s Pride and Okran’s Gulf. Shek Warriors and Hundred Guardians will start warring at those same regions as well. Valtena is defeated and the Holy Nation is in a panic. Loathsome. So gutless are the flatskins...But the Phoenix still holds his forces. He must die.Esata the Stone Golem Okran’s Shield gets taken over by Shek Kingdom once Valtena is killed, Okran’s Fist gets half-destroyed, and the HN army forces at Skimsands, Bast and Okran’s Valley get either removed or reduced significantly. The weak Okranites are lost without their precious Phoenix. Amusing... Such panic and squabbling amongst themselves has ended up destroying their own capital before we could take it. Good. I do not care for slaughtering feeble flatskin civilians. We have our own prizes to keep, the grass plains are ours and the Holy Nation is finally dead.You never fail to live up to your reputation, Battle Born. You and I have earned our place on the other side and we've restored Kral's glory once again. All shall fear the name of the Shek...You are a rival for Kral himself, Invincible (Player Name)!Esata the Stone Golem Holy Mines are now turned into tribute storages, and the farmers of Holy Farms have all their food taxed away from them as tributes now.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: I've heard much about you, (playername). Come, speak with me, child...Holy Lord Phoenix The Holy Nation Route is a World State Route where the player has allied relationship with The Holy Nation and initiated dialogue with Holy Lord Phoenix that opens up the questline for HN to change the state of Kenshi in a way that advances the HN’s interests. The HN route is diametrically opposed to Flotsam Ninjas Route and Shek Kingdom Route. The goal of this questline mainly revolves around purging Flotsam Ninjas and eradicating the Shek Kingdom (alongside some of their influential figures). While there are also other notable characters that are also of interest to HN, they are not included into the main dialogue, they are added into the “Secondary” or “Tertiary” targets based on their percieved importance and how much they align with HN’s goals. In order to initiate the dialogue with the Phoenix, the player must have at least +75 relations with HN, initiate as a speaker who is a human male without robotic limbs. Once that is done, the following lines will be said by the Phoenix: The Lord Of Light recognizes your good deeds, holy brother. The Lord sees all… Virtue is in your destiny, as it is my own. We are united, both, in our paths for greatness, for change and for goodness… Come! [He motions for you to come closer] [He gives you a bear hug and squeezes tight. There’s a potent smell of vegetables. He presses a thumb to your forehead] Bless this one, holy father. Protect him from all that may harm his spirit and body. Bless this one, holy father, my own brother… Here, take my gift with you. The Chalice of Fire, a beacon of light. May it ward you from darkness wherever your journey may take you. (Receives Chalice of Fire, +10 relation with HN) … Now, go forth, holy one! Continue your path… Main Targets (This part includes the targets that are directly referenced by the questline) After the initial opening lines are spoken, the player will unlock further dialogues with the Phoenix. To do so, the player simply has to reinitiate dialogue with the Phoenix. We have many enemies that plague us. Flotsam's Narko worshipping heretics still roam free and need to be brought to justice. They steal our child bearers and incite riots. And then there's the barbaric warmongering devils... They've terrorized our towns enough with their needless hunger for blood, the war must end.Holy Lord Phoenix Once this is spoken, you could ask for tips on how to destroy the Flotsam or SK, in either case, if you accept the task of destroying them, you will recieve a Holy Seal that allows you to call on Paladins for help (or sell it for a rather heft sum of 15k Cats). There is, rather ludicruously, no limits to how many times you can get the Holy Seal, and you could potentially get extremely rich just by repeatedly initiating dialogues and selling off Seals. (Technically speaking, it doesn’t really matter if you take down Flotsam Ninjas or Shek Kingdom first, outside of a few dialogue changes but for the sake of simplicity we will assume you will take down Moll first, since she is comparitively much easier to take down than SK.) Flotsam Ninjas Phoenix will tell you the rough location of where Flotsam are located (specifically at Hidden Forest), and the reason for why he doesn’t send army forces to vanquish them. Moll hides far away north west in the godless lands, the place of demons and monstrosities. Without her, the Flotsam order would fall apart. But where she hides, at home with the demons, I would not burden that journey upon any of my holy brothers.Holy Lord Phoenix Flotsam Ninjas will be defeated once Moll is ridden of, their settlement will become overrun with Cannibals. Shek Kingdom Once Moll is successfully captured or killed, the attention will move towards the Shek Kingdom. The holy plains are a safer place with Narko's spawn, Moll, out of the way... But the devil woman, Esata, she terrorizes us with her barbarian warmongerers. She bides her time, waiting to butcher us all in her centuries-old feud.Holy Lord Phoenix You could then ask for tips from Phoenix on how to successfully destroy SK, to which he will advise you to first take down Seto to enrage Esata. Since they are formidable opponents, he advises you to use Stealth (and probably Assassination) to get to her. The Golem may have demon strength but she has the weakness of an impulsive savage. We can trigger her wrecklessness by taking the thing she cherishes most, Seto, her demon child. Her warriors are erratic and violent, tackling them head on will be risky so you'd have to use stealth.Holy Lord Phoenix Once you capture/kill Seto, the following lines will be spoken. It's begun. With the devil child purged, the nest has been riled and the Golem's forces have already started warring in the holy plains. I pray for the southern cities... but the capital's defences are down at least. Our forces are on their way to Stenn. We can destroy the horned barbarians once and for all. The devil war will finally come to an end and we'll see peace again after hundreds of years...The Golem is vulnerable. Now is our time to attack.Holy Lord Phoenix This coincides largely with the World States that happen after Seto’s demise. Specifically, vengeful Hundred Guardian and Shek Warrior patrols (with more HG than that of a typical Shek patrol) will start invading Okran’s Gulf and Okran’s Pride, at the same time, HN will start exploiting the weakness of SK by sending forces into Border Zone and Stenn Desert (see their respective Zones for more details). Admag will have an override with weakened defenses, making further direct assaults into their capital easier. Post-Esata Shek Kingdom Clean Up (Editor’s Notes: Okay, this is where FCS becomes really messy and hard to read, and might actually be seriously broken. It appears that there are at least 3 conditions that are fulfilled when Esata is killed/imprisoned. One of which causes Phoenix to switch his attention to taking down Moll (even if Moll is already dead, the dialogue check seemingly forgot to check for the condition of Moll too), potentially making the dialogue with Phoenix hitting an infinite loop of switching between targeting Esata and Moll. The other 2 are conditions that also check for whether or not Flying Bull and Mukai are alive after Esata is dead, the dialogue mainly revolving around taking them down them too once Esata is dead. The oddity with those 2 conditions is that it could trigger if either one of them are dead, but not if they are both alive) Once Esata is taken down, Mukai will usurp the control of Shek Kingdom from Esata and govern Squin, Kamikaze patrols will spawn in Stenn Desert, and will likely be a hindrance to the holy army patrols there. If Flying Bull is killed, Phoenix will ask of you to kill Mukai. The Golem is destroyed only for another barbarian to take her place. The horned devils are fickle and easily won over with new leaders. I should have fores- I mean - I foresaw this in the Holy Flame, it is most unfortunate...The Mountain must be killed.Holy Lord Phoenix If Mukai is already taken down, Flying Bull will usurp the position from him and govern Squin. Posing as yet another threatening faction against HN. Phoenix will ask of you to kill FB too. The Golem is destroyed only for another barbarian to take her place! Predictably for men of such bloodlust, the horned hierarchy is a chaotic mess. This war is not over yet.Flying Bull must be killed.Holy Lord Phoenix Once FB is taken down too, there is (luckily) no more leaders of the Shek that need to be targeted. Squin will fall to the Berserkers, similar to how Admag fell to them too when Esata was out. All the Shek forces are now scattered and disorganized, posing no significant threat to the HN anymore. Absolver of the Inferno (HN victory ending) You have done so much already, holy one. Flotsam is gone and Okran's flame burns strong. The horned devils plague the Holy Lands but they are small in number, they won't last with their wreckless suicide mission. Eventually their kind will be extinct and we'll finally see peace.We will stay put on our greener pastures and spread our love for Okran. There is no more that can be done... Thanks to you, (player name), Absolver of the Infernal.Holy Lord Phoenix Congratulations, Absolver of the Inferno, the Light of Okran shines undisturbed at last. The shrieking of the Flotsam heretics has fallen silent, their dens of filth and rebellion reduced to ash and trash. No longer will our daughters and child-bearers be stolen from the fold by venomous tongues preaching lies of rebellion. They are returned to their rightful place — sanctified and disciplined under Okran’s watchful gaze. And the Shek… proud beasts broken upon the anvil of righteousness. Their bloodlust and godlessness served them no shield against Okran’s will. Their fortresses stand hollow, their war drums quiet, and their so-called warriors now beaten and bandaged, if they even yet live. The threat of the southern barbarism is no more — our borders are sanctified, our people secure. With these enemies of Okran cleansed, the world begins to heal and grow. Order is restored, and virtue reaffirmed. Okran’s chosen march forward, not merely as conquerors, but also as stewards — carrying the holy flame to purge the darkness, until none remain who would challenge His divine order. Nothing more can be done now… or is there? (look below) Secondary Targets (To be added, work to be done)

Anti-Slavers Ah yes, sir. Quite troublesome for production… The main leaders are hiding in the Forbidden Zone, south of the desert, we don’t know where exactly. articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: United Cities Route is a World State Route where the player has allied relationship with United Cities and having initiated dialogue with Emperor Tengu or Koin that opens up the questline for UC. The UC route is diametrically opposed to Rebel Farmers Route, Anti-Slavers Route. And comes into conflict with The Holy Nation Route, Shek Kingdom Route. It has elements of overlap with Traders Guild Route. The goal of this questline mainly revolves around crushing banditry and Anti-Slavers activity, while nudging HN forces out of their eastern border but still preserving them enough so that they can counter the Shek. The player can decide to speak with Tengu about quest matters, however, it will usually be re-directed to Koin instead, who will tell you which targets should be taken down. Primary Targets Rebel Farmers Bah! Way to sour my relaxation time, (player name). Talk to Koin about desert cleaning duties, I don't want my apetite spoiled thinking about those filthy dregs.Emperor Tengu, when asked about destorying the rebels Since Emperor Tengu is dismissive when talking about rebels, you will be redirected to Koin when talking about rebels, who will in turn state this. The rebel farmers, what an annoyance! They've not been tracked down yet, rumours suggest they run their little base of operations up north among the stick men and the cannibals.Koin, when asked about destroying rebel farmers The Stickmen and the Cannibals refer to Sinkuun and Darkfinger, respectively. Boss Simion (Rebel Farmer’s leader) is located in Fort Simion, which is located in Sinkuun. Take him out and the rebel farmers’ organization will cripple. Glad you got those rebel farmers out of our hair, (player name). Certainly makes my job a little easier. Now what can I do for you?Koin, Boss Simion defeated Many of Rebel Farmers squads will cease to spawn, with only the weaker ones remaining, representing a lower amount of banditry inside the UC desert areas. Anti-Slavers I can't give you much information on the Anti Slavers I'm afraid. Tinfist hides south in the Forbidden Zone, not the kind of unknown place you want to sacrifice too many soldiers to explore. His lackeys were sighted in Flats Lagoon and the ruins of the crags. Hiding is what they do best unfortunately. Cowards.Koin, when asked about destroying Anti-Slavers “Forbidden Zone” here refers to generally the entire southeast portion of the Kenshi map, which is too hazardous and wide to travel through, Tinfist himself is located specifically in Spring, at Stobe’s Gamble. Once Tinfist is down, the empire will expand their influence significantly, together with Traders Guild (see Tinfist’s world state section for more info). Good work with Tinfist, (player name).Koin, after Tinfist is defeated The Holy Nation The Holy Nation? Kill them all! Pain in the ass god chanters, they need to learn where they stand!-[...][He looks around the room at his expectant guards and sinks back into his throne][...] But bah! A fool I would be to involve myself in that petty little threeway between tribal bone warriors, flame worshipping kooks and yet another clan of ninja bandits... You think I want to deal with more ninjas after I've just cleaned my hands of Tinfist? Leave the Holy Nation where they are, they act as a nice little peaceable buffer between us and those bone loonies. Take down that inquisitor Vlahahlena and push them back at Okran's Shield, remind them who rules the world and take that lovely little defensive position of theirs. I'm sure they'll start sticking to themselves again and then we don't have to deal with those bloddthirsty boneheads knocking at our gates.Tengu, when asked about destroying THe Holy Nation after Tinfist is defeated Tengu mispronounces the name of High Inquisitor Valtena as Vlahahlena, which is promptly corrected by Koin. If you talk with Koin, he will tell you this: Well please don't goad the Emperor with such ideas. We need to be smart, (player name). If the western balance shifts too much in favour of the Shek then we'll have barbarian warlords pillaging in our desert in no time. The Holy Nation make a good distraction for the Shek... You want to keep Lord Tengu happy, give him Okran's Shield and he will be grateful to you. Once we push the Holy Nation back and take that defensive border position I'm sure they'll start sticking to themselves. Last thing they want are foreigners stepping foot in their precious holy plains anyway.Koin, when asked about destroying HN High Inquisitor Valtena is located in Okran’s Shield and is responsible largely for the military planning and organization at Bast and Skimsands. Once he is down, United Cities will be able to nudge the HN forces outside of those regions, capture Okran’s Shield, and gain a more stable territory hold there. Nice work with Okran's Shield, (player name). He may not show it but, I think the Emperor likes you... well, a little anyway...Koin, Valtena defeated Much or all of the HN forces at Bast and Skimsands will be reduced, representing the scattering of HN forces after Valtena was knocked out, giving UC the greater advantage. National Hero of the Empire (UC Victory Ending) Tinfist is out of the picture, Simion is gone, and the Holy Nation has been pushed back. The desert flourishes and our enemies are crushed. You're the hero of our Empire, (player name)Koin speaking after Tinfist, Simion, Valtena all defeated.

You are hereby arrested for illegal activity within Empire land.Samurai War Leader Drug Bust is an event that can trigger if a member of the United Cities military or police sees an illegal building owned by the player. These buildings include Biofuel Distillery (Hemp), Hemp Farm, Hemp Processor, and Hydroponic Hemp. Emperor Tengu must also not be killed or captured for the event to trigger. Once the illegal building is spotted, there are a few potential routes the dialog could take, depending on whether or not it is inside an NPC owned town, as well as the Personality of the Samurai who spotted it. A Smart, Honorable, or Fearful personality Samurai if inside an NPC town will immediately assign a bounty of c.2,000 to the one or more player characters and attempt to arrest them. If not inside an NPC town, they will leave and report back to their superiors, which will trigger this event in 12-28 hours. If the player’s squad is less than 9 characters, then the Samurai will immediately assign the bounty and attack even outside an NPC town. A Traitorous, Dumb, Brave, or Maniacal personality Samurai will attempt to extort the player. If the player ignores them, the Samurai will eventually assign a bounty of c.2,000 to the player and attack them. If talked to there are many routes you can take. Accepting to pay them a bribe of c.2,000 will result in them attempting to extort you for an extra c.1,000. If you lack the funds to pay the full c.3,000, then they’ll let you off with just the c.2,000. Insisting on paying only the c.2,000 has a chance to convince them to take it and leave, and a chance they might attack and assign the bounty. If they choose to attack, but the player has more than 7 characters in their squad, the Samurai will instead report to his superiors, and this event will trigger in 48-72 hours. Refusal to pay or taunting/mocking them will result in them immediately attacking your characters and assigning the bounty, unless the player has more than 7 characters in their squad, in which case the Samurai will instead report back to HQ and this event will trigger in 48-72 hours. Alternatively, you can attempt to convince the Samurai you are someone of importance. Claiming you are a noble will only work if your outpost is level 3 or higher (the big town icon on the map), if your base is any lower level then they will simply attack or trigger the event. If you’ve killed (not captured) the Bugmaster or the Holy Lord Phoenix, or if you’ve killed/captured Esata the Stone Golem or Tinfist, you can attempt to intimidate them into leaving you alone, though this only has a chance to work and will trigger the attack and bounty or event if it fails. If the event is triggered, the United Cities will send an assault to your base. This assault will consist of 1-3 squads, each made up of 1-3 Samurai Scouts, 2-5 Samurai, and 10-20 Samurai Conscripts, and will be led by an additional Samurai. There is a very low chance that one or more of the squads will be substituted for a different squad, made up of 1-3 Samurai Scouts, 5-8 Samurai, and 1-4 Samurai Conscripts, led by a Samurai Sergeant. Once the assault arrives the war leader will make a short speech about being here to arrest you and then order their soldiers to attack. If victorious, the assault will leave shortly after winning. If defeated, the United Cities Assault event will trigger in 72-100 hours.

(35 individuals set) The squad composition will have 1 Eyegore, 1 Samurai Captain, 2 Samurai Sergeants, 3 Samurai Heavies, 1 Samurai Scout, 10 Samurai. The remaining squads have two possible variants they can spawn as. With the 1st one spawning more frequently than the latter. 1 Samurai Sergeant, 1-3 Samurai Scouts, 10-15 Samurai, 8-20 Samurai Conscripts. 1 Samurai Sergeant, 1-3 Samurai Scouts, 5-8 Samurai, 1-4 Samurai Conscripts. Once the assault arrives Eyegore and his Samurai will have a short conversation, usually differing depending on the trigger source or faction relations. And then Eyegore and his soldiers will attack. If victorious, the assault should leave the base shortly afterward. If defeated and it was a Longen or Tengu trigger, there will be a 40% chance to trigger an Elite Hunter Assault in 24-72 hours. If it was a retaliation trigger, nothing else will trigger.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: The Inquisitorium has received reports of wild women running loose in this place...War Leader Paladin Holy Nation Assault (Minor), simply referred to as ‘Holy Nation Assault’ in-game, is an event that can occur if the player failed to fulfil Prayer Day requirements (Refusing to pray, not having the Holy Flame, having no men, or speaking to them with a non-human), or was seen by patrols that the outpost built in their territory goes against The Holy Nation interests (i.e Having only women in the outpost, or having non-humans in the outpost) and failed to pacify the patrol commander. It is closely related to, but not to be confused with, two other events of the same name, Holy Nation Assault (Major), and Holy Nation Assault (Inquisitor). The event cannot trigger if the Holy Lord Phoenix has been killed or captured in the case of the Prayer Day retaliation, while the race and women triggered variants require the Holy Lord Phoenix, High Inquisitor Seta, and High Inquisitor Valtena to be killed or captured in order to be stopped. After the requirements above are met, The Holy Nation will send an assault in 10-48 hours depending on the trigger used, this patrol will consist of 3-4 Paladins, 5 Holy Sentinels and 10-15 Holy Chosen with one additional Paladin acting as the War Leader for this event. After the War Leader has arrived to the designated players outpost he will then give a speech about the reason of attacking and say the player will be ‘disciplined’, during which the player might have a final chance to prevent the conflict if they have a human male and the original trigger was for only having women at the outpost, at which point the raid will be cancelled and Prayer Day will launch in 150 to 160 hours. If not pacified this patrol will then proceed to attack the outpost and the player characters inside it. If the raid is victorious, they will occupy the player’s base, patrolling around it, using the furniture, freeing captives, and imprisoning your characters. If the raid is defeated, there is a 100% chance to trigger a Holy Nation Assault (Major) event 72 to 110 hours afterward.

We protect your back, you share your profits.Hound Hound Check In is an Event that can occur if the player has an outpost within 4,500 meters of Rot, Big Grim is still alive and free, and the player is allied to the Hounds faction. If the conditions are fulfilled, the event has a 20% chance to occur each day if the player is within 3,000 meters, this chance scale down with distance until it hits 0% at 4,500 meters. Once triggered, the Hounds will send a campaign to the player’s outpost. This campaign will consist of two squads, each made up of 6 Hounds. Once the campaign arrives, they will give a short speech asking the player to come speak with them. If ignored, the leader will decide you must be busy and return again in 70-85 hours. If spoken to, the leader will demand that you pay them “Big Grim’s cut”, which is c.2,000. Accepting to pay will trigger another instance of this event in 150-175 hours. Saying you can’t afford the cost will grant one-time a short reprieve, they will return in 60-70 hours. Refusing to pay, saying you can’t afford it a second time, or ignoring two consecutive campaigns, will result in the campaign assaulting the base and breaking the alliance with the Hounds faction. If the assault is victorious, a Stone Rat Visit event will be triggered in 95-110 hours. If the assault is defeated, it will trigger a Revenge of the Hounds event in 12-36 hours. Like most tax Events, if the campaign is defeated by a third-party faction like bandits or wild animals on the way to the player’s outpost, it will prevent any future tax visits from the faction until the player’s next import. This is due to the long repeat limit timer, and the fact that it doesn’t consider being defeated by a third party as the player killing them. This can be exploited by purposefully luring hostiles to the event’s forces while they en route to the player’s base.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: For what you did to our comrade, you don't get the privilege of mercy...Anti-Slaver Jonin Assault is a series of Events that can trigger as a result of the Player killing or capturing certain Anti-Slavers characters. There are technically three variants to this event, though one cannot trigger naturally thanks to a bug. The first variant can trigger if the player is an enemy of the Anti-Slavers, has killed or captured Bo, Jaegar, and Grey, while Tinfist is still alive and free. It has a 25% chance to trigger each day if within 7,000 meters of Spring, which scales down with distance until hitting 0% chance at 15,000 meters. The assault party consists of 3-5 squads, each is most often made up of 5 Anti-Slavers and 5 Anti-Slaver (Unarmed), or rarely 5 Anti-Slaver Jonins instead. If defeated, it is supposed to have a 40% to trigger the third variant in 72-100 hours, but this normally fails due to it requiring Grey to be alive and free. The second variant triggers if the player has killed or captured Tinfist, but Jaegar is still alive and free. It has a 100% chance to trigger each day if within 8,000 meters of Spring, this chance scales down with distance until hitting 0% at 20,000 meters. The assault party consists of 3-4 squads, each most commonly made up of 5 Anti-Slaver Jonins, but less commonly can have 5 Anti-Slavers and 5 Anti-Slaver (Unarmed) instead, while it is led by Jaegar. It is supposed to be able to be led by Grey and Bo as well, but this cannot trigger in vanilla thanks to a bug. The third variant, which is bugged and cannot trigger normally, is supposed to trigger as a result of defeating the first variant, but as it requires Grey to be alive and free, while the first variant requires him to be killed or captured it cannot trigger (unless the player captures him then frees him later before this variant is triggered). The assault party consists of 3-4 squads, the first made up of 4 Anti-Slaver (Unarmed), 4 Anti-Slaver Jonins, Tinfist, and Grey. The others will be most commonly made up of 5 Anti-Slaver Jonins, but less commonly can have 5 Anti-Slavers and 5 Anti-Slaver (Unarmed) instead. If defeated, it should have a 20% chance of triggering the 3rd variant again in 24-72 hours, this of course still requires Grey to be alive and free though.

Either you can pay us tribute from your stores, or we run this outpost to the ground. Your choice, flatskin.Shek Warrior War Leader Food Tribute is the first outpost visit sent by Shek Kingdom to challenge the player to a fight or alternatively rob the food supplies of people that settled up in their territory by force. It can trigger as long as the player’s base is within 1,500 Meters of a Shek Kingdom settlement and that Bugmaster, Phoenix, Bayan, Seto, and Esata have all not been killed or captured, and that the player is not an ally nor an enemy of the Shek Kingdom. It will have a 15% chance to trigger each day if within 1,000 meters of a Shek Kingdom owned location, this chance will reduce with any distance farther than that, until it hits a 0% chance at 1,500 meters away. Once triggered the Shek Kingdom will send the campaign to the player’s base, this campaign will consist of 0-1 Shek Scouts and 6 - 9 Shek Warriors. Once the campaign arrives, the leader will shout at the player to come talk. If the player ignores the leader, the campaign will leave and the Return For Blood event will be triggered in 12-24 hours. Once speaking to the leader, there will be a few options. If you accept the tribute demands they will begin taking food from any food storage containers in the base, and Return For Tribute will trigger in 120-250 hours. If you attempt to negotiate, they will insist that they set the terms, refusal at this point will result in them leaving and Return For Blood triggering in 24-30 hours. And finally, if you challenge them, they will leave and Return For Blood will trigger in 24-30 hours, in addition you will receive a small +1 relations with the Shek Kingdom. If the tribute is accepted, each Shek will take roughly 10 items of food. For reference, if all the foodstuff they take is Bread, it will cost the player up to around c.40,000 in value on average to fully fulfill their inventory. Arguably, the Tribute Round is the most expensive of all tax events, as the foodstuff they take could very easily exceed Tax Man Visit at even the bare minimum of food supplies of 3 Ration Packs. This could also potentially have zero impact if the player exploits the event, since mechanically Sheks (much like Starving Bandits) can’t actually sense food placed on the ground. Like most tax Events, if the campaign is defeated by a third-party faction like bandits or wild animals on the way to the player’s outpost, it will prevent any future tax visits from the faction until the player’s next import. This is due to the long repeat limit timer, and the fact that it doesn’t consider being defeated by a third party as the player killing them. This can be exploited by purposefully luring hostiles to the event’s forces while they en route to the player’s base. Though in the case of the Shek Kingdom here, it is possible to reactivate the tribute events by failing to defeat a Shek Challengers event. Tips This event can be cheese-able by emptying all storages containing food before they reach the players outpost. !!! It is unfeasible to to ally with Shek Kingdom through tributes, since relations tend to decrease whenever a member of a faction is harmed, downed, or killed.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Under order of the Empire you have been sentenced for multiple crimes of treason. By punishment of death.Samurai United Cities Assault is an Event sent by the United Cities as a response to losing the Drug Bust, Tax Evasion Enforcement, or United Cities Assault events. Except as a response to tax evasion, it cannot trigger if Emperor Tengu, Lord Inaba, Lord Nagata, Lord Yoshinaga, Lady Sanda, and Lady Tsugi are all killed or captured. Once triggered, the United Cities will send an assault party. This party will consist of at least two squads, made up of 10-20 Samurai Conscripts, 2-5 Samurai, and 1-3 Samurai Scouts, led by an additional Samurai. Rarely one or more of the squads will be substituted for a squad made up of 1-4 Samurai Conscripts, 5-8 Samurai, and 1-3 Samurai Scouts, led by a Samurai Sergeant. Once the assault party arrives, the War Leader will give a short speech, then order the assault to begin. The soldiers will then attack the gates, attack any player characters they see, and liberate captives they find. If the assault is defeated, it will trigger another United Cities Assault event in 72-100 hours, with a 100% chance if this event was triggered by the Drug Bust event, and a 50% chance if it was triggered any other way. If the player is defeated, the assault party will retreat and return home, the Tax Collector event will be triggered in 12-48 hours if this event was triggered by the Tax Evasion Enforcement event, otherwise no further events will be triggered.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Lord Longen sends his respects today! My squadron is at your disposal, sirs...Samurai Sergeant United Cities Reinforcements is an Event that will trigger in response to the Holy Assault, Holy Nation Assault (Inquisitor), Jonin Assault, Retribution Of God, and Wrath Of God events, as long as the Player is an ally of the United Cities and Emperor Tengu is alive and free, and the player is NOT an ally of the Anti-Slavers, Holy Nation, or Shek Kingdom. Once triggered the United Cities will send reinforcements from the location they own closest to the player’s Base. While they will move faster than most hostile events, they can still arrive too late if the player’s base is closer to the hostile event’s spawn location than to the origin of the reinforcements. These reinforcements will consist of 1-2 squads, each made up of 1-4 Samurai Conscripts, 5-8 Samurai, 1-3 Samurai Scouts, led by a Samurai Sergeant. Once the reinforcements arrive, they will give a short speech, and then start patrolling the player’s base, attacking hostiles, defending the player’s characters, and healing wounded allies.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: You've commited the gravest of crimes against Okran... Spawn of Narko herself, I will vanquish you and restore peace in our blessed nation! Burn him, him sent from the dark demoness herself! He must be purged to ash for bringing harm to our beloved Holy Lord Phoenix! Blessed be his name!High Inquisitor Seta The Wrath of God is a recurring Holy Nation base assault event that is launched once a player takes down Holy Lord Phoenix or defeated Retribution of God. It technically has a max range of 90,000 meters, and a “near” range of 50,000 meters, but both are far larger than the map itself, meaning that the initial event has a 100% of triggering each day no matter where in Kenshi’s map you live. Normally the event will be led by Seta, and he is required for the initial event to trigger (Note: There is a variant that is meant to have Valtena, which is supposed to trigger after Seta has been killed or captured, but in vanilla this is bugged and will not trigger due to Seta being set as the leader). Subsequent triggers of the event by defeating it do not require Seta to have survived, though the assaults will cease unless you’ve defeated Valtena before triggering the event (due to the aforementioned bug with his variants not triggering). This event has three main variants, with the second triggering after defeating the first, and the third triggering after defeating the second, with the third having a high chance to repeat after each defeat. The squads would be summed up to have 80 individuals in total. The first initial variant, will be led by High Inquisitor Seta, followed by 5 Paladins and 3 Inquisitors. He will also be accompanied by 3 ~ 5 squads each consisting of: 1 Inquisitor, 1-2 High Paladins, 10-12 Paladins, and 4-9 Holy Servants. If defeated, the second variant will trigger in 30-60 hours (~1.9 days), assuming Seta is still okay, or both he and Valtena have been killed or captured. The second variant will be led by either Seta, or one of the normal Inquisitors. Seta will bring his entourage of 5 Paladins and 3 Inqusitors if he joins the assault. Otherwise, the assault forces will consist of 3 ~ 4 squads each consisting of 1 Inquisitor, 1-2 High Paladins, 10-12 Paladins, and 4-9 Holy Servants. If defeated, it has a 95% of triggering the third variant in 36-80 hours (~2.4 days). If Seta has been killed or captured, but Valtena has not, the third variant will trigger, but will fail when the timer reaches 0. The third and final variant will be led by either Seta, or one of the normal Inquisitors. Seta will bring his entourage of 5 Paladins and 3 Inqusitors if he joins the assault. Otherwise, the assault forces will consist of 3 ~ 5 squads each consisting of 1 Inquisitor, 1-2 High Paladins, 10-12 Paladins, and 4-9 Holy Servants. If defeated, and as long as Seta has not been killed or captured, it will have a 100% chance of repeating the third event again in 168-672 hours. If High Inquisitor Seta has been killed or captured, but High Inquisitor Valtena has not, the event will trigger again but will fail (due to bug) when the timer reaches 0. If both have been killed or captured, there is a 95% chance of repeating in 168-672 hours (~17.5 days). Trivia This event is known in the FCS as: First Variant “HN Assault (Phoenix kidnap)” “HN Assault (Phoenix kidnap) valtena alive” “HN Assault (Phoenix kidnap) seta alive” “HN Assault (killed phoenix)” “HN Assault (killed phoenix) seta alive” “HN Assault (killed phoenix) valtena alive” Second Variant “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger1)” “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger1) seta alive” “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger1) valtena alive” “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger1) inquistors dead” Third Variant “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger2)” “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger2) seta alive” “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger2) valtena alive” “HN Assault (ultimate) (trigger2) inquisitors dead” The assaults are set to have 80/60/75 individuals spawned for the 1st/2nd/3rd variant, respectively. This event has the largest amount of individuals of any assaults, tied with Eyegore’s Assault (only of Tengu variant) and Hive Attack (Western Hive). This is the only assault that encompasses the entire map that can be launched repetitively without the need for any leader(s) to be alive, making The Holy Nation the only faction that can unceasingly assault the Player Base with 100% chance to launch anywhere every day.
